1 رَثَدَ المَتَاعَ , (T, S, M, A, K,) aor.
رَثُدَ , inf. n. رَثْدٌ; (S, M;) and ↓ ارتثدهُ , (K,) in some copies of the K ↓ ارثدهُ [which I doubt not to be a mistranscription]; (TA;) He put the goods, or household goods, or utensils and furniture, one upon another, or together, in regular order, or compactly, (T, S, M, A, K,) or side by side. (S.) ―
-b2- رَثَدَتْ بَيْضَهَا She (a hen) collected together her eggs. (IAar, M.) ―
-b3- رُثِدَتِ القَصْعَةُ بِالثَّرِيدِ The bowl was heaped with the ثريد [or crumbled, or broken, bread, moistened with broth,] put together and made even. (M, L.) ―
-b4- رَثَدَ حَاجَتَهُ (assumed tropical:) He deferred, delayed, postponed, or put off, his (another's) needful affairs; the sing. noun being used for the pl. (L, from a trad.) ＝
-A2- رَثِدَ, aor.
رَثَدَ , (K,) inf. n. رَثَدٌ; (TK;) and ↓ ارثد ; i. q. كَدِرَ; (K;) said of a man [as meaning He was, or became, disturbed, perturbed, or troubled, in mind]; (TA;) or said of water [as meaning it was, or became, turbid, thick, or muddy.] (TK.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
